source.work: Augustine, De doctrina christiana, Book II, chapters 1–3, paragraphs 1–4
source.license: The Georgetown page does not state a license; translation licensing is therefore recorded as unknown. The Latin parallel is public-domain text, but no byte hash was used here.
source.owned_span: II.1.1–II.3.4: definition of sign; natural signs; conventional signs; human visual/auditory signs and words.

complete_paraphrase.content: A sign is a thing that, beyond its sensory appearance, brings another thing to mind. Footprint indicates an animal has passed; smoke indicates fire; a living voice indicates mental feeling; a trumpet tells soldiers to advance, retreat, or perform what the battle requires.

Natural signs lead to knowledge of another thing without intention: smoke/fire, footprint/passed animal, and countenance/mental emotion. The work notes this class but sets it aside for the present discussion.

Conventional signs are exchanged by living beings to convey perceptions, thoughts, or feelings. Animal calls are given as examples: a cock signals food to a hen and doves call mates. Whether every animal cry is intentional is left outside the present scope.

Human signs address sight or hearing: nods, hand/body movements, military standards and flags, bugle/flute/lyre, and especially words. The sensory channel and convention determine how a sign communicates.

typed_distinctions.scope_rule: A natural sign maps through observed cause/effect; a conventional sign maps through shared use and may require audience context.
typed_distinctions.reused_operation: SIGN(sign) -> referent/content is reused across footprint, smoke, voice, trumpet, animal calls, flags, and words, but its argument type changes from physical cause to convention/audience.

worked_consequence.source_case_a: SMOKE -> FIRE_PRESENT; no intentional signaler is required.
worked_consequence.source_case_b: TRUMPET + battle_state -> ADVANCE or RETREAT; the physical sound is insufficient without conventional context.
worked_consequence.serious_rival: Treat natural/conventional as descriptive metadata only and route every sign through one context-independent label lookup. This keeps the source examples but makes trumpet action fixed and erases the natural-cause/conventional-use distinction.
worked_consequence.smallest_later_test: A complete later passage would need one reused sign operation with a physical-cause context and a conventional audience/action context, then a changed result under the latter while preserving the former.

limits: This is a pedagogical semiotic taxonomy, not a report of one historical event.
The source excludes whether some animal calls are intentional, so that branch is not filled.
No manuscript sign or word meaning is supplied.
